newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas grain, soy harvests still ahead of normal.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas grain, soy harvests still ahead of normal.

text.p: Arkansas's soybean, cotton, corn, sorghum and rice harvests were all running ahead of normal as of Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

Soybeans were 17 percent harvested, up from 10 percent a week earlier, eight percent last year and a five-year average pace of 11 percent. The crop was 31 percent mature, up from 19 percent last year and a five-year average of 21 percent.
Rice was 87 percent harvested, also ahead of last year's 81 percent and the average of 78 percent, with cotton 29 percent harvested versus 27 and 25 percent respectively.
Corn was 96 percent harvested, up from an average 94 percent, and sorghum 90 percent, versus the normal 85 percent.
"Numerous counties reported rice, corn and sorghum harvests were winding down," the report said.
Wheat planting was also reported in several counties.
The crop was 10 percent planted and five percent emerged, up from the average pace of nine and two percent respectively, the report indicated.
